newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Swedish insurer Trygg extends cuts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swedish insurer Trygg extends cuts.

text.p: Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa AB on Friday reported a slight rise in nine-month profits but said further cost-cutting was needed to maintain profitability in the increasingly competitive finance sector.
Trygg-Hansa, Sweden's second biggest insurer after Skandia, reported a pre-tax profit of 2.10 billion crowns ($317 million) for the nine months to September 30 versus 2.09 billion a year ago.

Finance director Lars Lundquist said the pace of cuts already started by the company would continue for at least the next three to five years to ensure its position in the competitive sector that is on the brink of restructuring.

"We wouldn't at this moment say that our cost cuttings will be able to carry forward into the profit and loss account as a margin increase but certainly we believe we will be able to keep our competitiveness and profitability," he told Reuters.

Analysts said the nine-month result was much as expected, if not a little better, with non-life insurance pre-tax profits rising to 583 million crowns from 479 million while other operations slipped to 1.52 billion crowns against 1.61 billion.
The company posted gross premiums of 8.53 billion crowns compared to 8.56 billion a year earlier.
"It made more in net profit than we had forecast for the year," Goldman Sachs analyst Giovanni Govi told Reuters.
He said the report included an unexpectedly good underwriting result with a net combined ratio of 107.4 percent compared to 109.3 percent this time last year.
Another unexpected boost for Trygg-Hansa was the strong performance of the Stockholm bourse with its shares rising from 110 crowns in early September to 133 crowns on Friday.
"Part of the share price performance reflects the fact that the market is expecting more restructuring and consolidation in the Swedish finance sector," Govi said.
"But I'm not sure it can keep up outperforming the market," said Govi, who current sees Trygg-Hansa as a market performer.
But Mikael Garton from Swedish brokerage Ohman said the rise in the share price prompted his company on Friday to downgrade is trading recommendation to neutral from outperform.
"The share prices has grown a lot in the past month and we think it is near top levels now," Garton told Reuters.
The restructuring of Sweden's finance sector has been a key theme in the market this year with several moves mooted.
Lundquist said the sector needed to be restructured because there were currently too many players.
"We are moving into each other's industries, banks and insurance companies," he said.
In May Trygg-Hansa failed in an attempted hostile takeover bid for Swedish insurance group Wasa but Lundquist said there were no immediate plans for further acquisitions.
"We have stated very clearly that we believe restructuring of the finance industry in Sweden would be healthy but we are not entertaining any immediate plans," he said.
Analysts said Trygg-Hansa, which held a 19.2 percent stake in Sweden's life insurance market in 1995 and a 14.9 percent one in non-life insurance, had been aggressive in cutting costs to date.
The company had 3,179 employees at the start of 1996 but as of September 30 had 3,050. Total operating costs for the period declined to 872 million crowns from 994 million. ($1=6.63 crowns)
